screen: S7 · Settings · root vs the 39 detail/state boards
verdict: UNSURE(two models cannot both be right; one set must be redrawn)
finding: The module draws two incompatible navigation models for the same 13 items: a full-width two-column card grid with no rail (root), and a persistent 140px left nav + 1240px pane with the rail (every other board) — and the shipped code is neither of those two-pane layouts, it is a drill-in stack.
evidence: Measured geometry: 1688:7195 Middle band = rows at x=40 w=560 and x=640 w=560, no Rail child. 638:2378 Middle band = Rail x=0 w=60 + 'Settings nav (140)' x=60 w=140 + 'Settings pane' x=200 w=1240. Code: SettingsTab.tsx:288 isRoot state; :829-831 root screen gets aria-hidden/inert when drilled in; settings.css:24-33 both screens are position:absolute inset:0 on one plane; :61-67 .bd-set-snav is flex:1 root-screen content, not a column. 39 of 45 boards (12 detail + 26 states + 1 locked) draw the persistent-nav model.
recommend: Redraw the 39 detail/state boards as the drill-in section screen (DrillInHeader breadcrumb + single column) and keep 1688:7195 as the root, or amend the code — but the file must carry ONE model.

verdict: KEEP(as the model of record — but the boards contradict it)
finding: The module's own founder-locked note states 'One column, drawer width — never a two-pane master-detail', and 39 boards draw exactly the two-pane master-detail it forbids. The note is marked RETIRED, but nothing in the file records what replaced it.
evidence: 1344:7162 text: 'Settings navigate by DRILL-IN, not master-detail … Clicking a row slides its screen IN over the list, with a ‹ back header. One column, drawer width — never a two-pane master-detail.' The note also claims drawer width 280-320px, which is stale: rail/tabsConfig.ts:196-199 records Settings graduating from a 320px drawer to mode:'fullpage'. So the WIDTH claim is dead but the MODEL claim is still what the code implements (SettingsTab.tsx:400-439 push / :473-493 pop / :870-879 DrillInHeader).
recommend: Rename the note to record what is still binding ('drill-in model KEPT, drawer-width claim superseded 2026-08-?? by fullpage') instead of a blanket RETIRED, so the next reader does not treat the master-detail boards as approved.

finding: The root board cites SettingsTab.tsx:75-92 but omits three things the shipped root has: the WORKSPACE group (Members ↗ / Billing ↗), the Tour row, and the Pro badge that marks locked rows before you click them.
evidence: 1688:7195 text ends at 'Webhooks'; no WORKSPACE, no Tour, no Pro. Code: SettingsTab.tsx:841-844 renders the WORKSPACE group with an 'opens dashboard ↗' hint, :845-856 the Tour row, :767 the per-row Pro badge. All 12 detail boards DO draw WORKSPACE / Members ↗ / Billing ↗ (e.g. 638:2378), so the root is the odd one out inside its own module.
recommend: Add the WORKSPACE group, the Tour row and Pro badges to the root board; without the badge the user only discovers a paywall after a click.

verdict: MERGE-INTO(927:4474 — make it a WORKSPACE ↗ row)
finding: Webhooks is workspace-scoped and admin-only by its own copy, yet it sits inside SITE settings in the editor — breaking the principle this module already states on its own interstitial board.
evidence: 640:3849 subtitle 'Workspace event deliveries'; 1703:9694 body 'One endpoint per workspace'; 1703:10352 forbidden state 'Only an admin can manage webhooks … Ask a workspace admin'. 927:4474 (this module's own exit interstitial) says: 'Members, billing and team permissions are workspace-level — they are not part of this site's settings, and not part of the Editor.' Code agrees on scope (WebhooksScreen.tsx:94-97 permission-denied branch) and there is no dashboard webhooks route.
recommend: Demote the Webhooks nav row to a WORKSPACE ↗ deep-link alongside Members and Billing, and build the surface where the other workspace-level admin surfaces live.

verdict: CUT(from the editor; keep a WORKSPACE ↗ row)
finding: The board designs a working connected-integrations manager (Stripe/Mailchimp CONNECTED with Manage, ConvertKit/Zapier/Netlify with Connect) for a screen that in the product is six static 'soon' link-outs, while the real OAuth surface is in the dashboard.
evidence: 640:3488 text: 'CONNECTED · Stripe · Payments · checkout sessions · CONNECTED · Manage …'. Code: IntegrationsScreen.tsx:38 every row is status='soon'; the working connect flow is packages/dashboard/app/dashboard/settings/integrations/page.tsx:8 → integrations-content.tsx:193-209, and /dashboard/marketplace (page.tsx:43,57-68) has ZERO editor callers of marketplace.*.
recommend: Either point the Integrations row at the dashboard (↗, like Members/Billing) or move this board to the dashboard module; do not board an in-editor manager the editor does not own.

finding: 'Headers' is a hosting/security implementation concept, not an object in the user's mental model (site → pages → elements → brand → publish): the screen's primary control is a raw CSP header textarea. The product itself already conflates it with Custom code.
evidence: 640:2789 content: 'CSP header value: default-src \'self\'; img-src …', 'X-FRAME-OPTIONS · SAMEORIGIN', 'HSTS · Max age · 2 years'. Proof of the conflation: 1138:13436, the Custom code Pro-lock, carries Headers' subtitle ('CSP, HSTS, security policy') and Headers' body copy. Headers is also the only settings subject with a single door and no dashboard equivalent (0 hits for hsts/CSP across packages/dashboard/app + components).
recommend: Fold Headers into Custom code (639:4144) as an 'Advanced · security' block behind a disclosure, cutting the 13-row nav to 12 and removing the screen most likely to be opened by mistake.

verdict: UNSURE(split: config is a setting, the inbox is not)
finding: One screen carries two jobs with opposite frequencies — a once-ever provider config and a submissions inbox the user returns to daily — and the inbox already has a second, fuller door in the dashboard.
evidence: 640:3135 stacks PROVIDER (provider, endpoint, spam) above SUBMISSIONS (3 rows, NEW/DELIVERED). The screenshot shows the inbox is read-only: no row opens, no reply, no delete, no filter, no pagination, and the header slot that holds 'Save changes' on every sibling screen holds 'Export CSV' here. Second door: packages/dashboard/app/dashboard/sites/[id]/feedback/page.tsx:13 + submissions-panel.tsx call the same tRPC procedures.
recommend: Pick one home for the inbox (the dashboard reads like the right one) and leave Settings › Forms with provider config plus a link; if the editor keeps it, the inbox needs a detail view — reading a submission is the job.

finding: The board draws a full export configurator inside Settings (Output format, Include assets, Minify, Inline critical CSS, index.html preview, Download .zip), but Export in the product is a modal with four other doors, and the Settings screen is a three-line signpost.
evidence: 639:2754 content listed above. Code: SettingsTab.tsx:728-740 renders a signpost + 'Open exporter' button; the modal is shell/StudioModals.tsx:166 and is reached from engine/commands/defaultCommands.ts:437-442 (Ctrl+Shift+E), SiteMenu.tsx:211, StudioHeader.tsx:815 and useComposerInit.ts:447.
recommend: Board the exporter once, as the modal, and reduce this board to the signpost row the code ships — otherwise the fifth door gets built as a second editor.

finding: A second door to project metadata: this modal and Settings › General write the same field under two different labels, and the modal is what ⌘, and the Site menu actually open — so the 45-board Settings module is not the surface most users will reach for 'site settings'.
evidence: 1172:4867 fields: PROJECT NAME, AUTHOR/DESCRIPTION, Canvas tab (grid size + snap), SEO tab (default site title). Code: ProjectSettingsModal.tsx:223-231 'Site name (social sharing)' writes seo.siteName (:117-124) — the byte-identical target of Settings › General 'Site Name' (SiteSettingsScreen.tsx:115-122). Both doors open the MODAL: useEditorShortcuts.ts:119-122 (⌃,) and SiteMenu.tsx:193-197 ('Site settings'); the 45-board tab is only on rail shortcut S (tabsConfig.ts:187-200).
recommend: Delete the duplicate field from one side. Grid size / snap-to-grid have their ONLY door in this modal, so keep the modal as a canvas-preferences dialog and rename it away from 'Site settings'.

verdict: KEEP(the pointer is right; its claim is not)
finding: The pointer board says brand lives in ONE place; the code says two, ships a five-row field map, and calls the destination panel by a third name.
evidence: 1344:7165 text: 'Brand lives in the Brand panel … edited in one place so nothing drifts' and 'Supersedes the full field-map drawing.' Code: SettingsTab.tsx:135-138 comment 'Branding spans two canonical homes: the Palette tab owns design tokens … and the General section owns site identity (favicon, social links)'; BRANDING_FIELD_MAP :148-154 has five rows with jumps to General and SEO; the CTA reads 'Open Palette →' (:200-210). The panel is labelled 'Brand' in the rail (tabsConfig.ts:179), 'Styles' as a tool (:312), 'Palette' in Settings, 'Brand' in SiteMenu.tsx:249.
recommend: Decide whether brand is one home or two and make board and code agree; and settle on ONE name — the rail says Brand, so Settings should too.

verdict: UNSURE(needs a product decision, not a redraw)
finding: Three surfaces claim the favicon and the design never says which wins: the Branding nav subtitle promises it, the Branding pointer omits it, and the field actually sits in General.
evidence: Nav subtitle 'Colors, type, favicon' (1688:7195 and SettingsTab.tsx:78); 1344:7165 lists only 'Fonts, colors, logo and design tokens'; 638:2378 has 'Favicon URL · /assets/favicon.ico' under SITE IDENTITY. In code the split is worse: the editor field writes projectSettings.seo.favicon (SiteSettingsScreen.tsx:123-130) while the dashboard uploads to the Site.favicon column (site-detail/settings-tab.tsx:209-231); BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:140-150,180-195 mirrors touchIcon but NOT favicon, and lib/publish-html.ts:58-59 injects the column value only when no rel=icon exists — so a dashboard-uploaded favicon is silently discarded.
recommend: Name one canonical favicon home on the boards and align the three subtitles to it; a design that says 'favicon' in three places is what produced two stores in code.

finding: The Pro lock screen for Custom code describes a different feature: its subtitle and body are Headers' copy. A user hitting the paywall is told they are buying CSP and HSTS.
evidence: 1138:13436 renders title 'Custom code' with subtitle 'CSP, HSTS, security policy' and body 'Custom code is a Pro feature — Set CSP, HSTS and frame policy on your own domain.' Compare 639:4144, whose real subtitle is 'Head, body, CSS injections'. Verified in the board screenshot, not inferred.
recommend: Rewrite to the Custom code job ('Inject scripts and CSS into every page'), and state the current plan and the price — the screen has two Upgrade CTAs and neither says what it costs.

finding: Two error states ship developer-environment copy as user-facing text: they ask the customer whether their dev server is running.
evidence: 1702:7261 pane text: 'Couldn\'t load domains. Is the dashboard running?' 1703:10022: 'Couldn\'t load the webhook. Is the dashboard running?' Both are rendered as plain body text with no icon, no alert treatment, and no retry (screenshot of 1702:7261 confirms). In code these two screens render errors into .bd-set-section-d, an 11px muted section-subtitle style with no role='alert' (DomainsScreen.tsx:211-212,242; WebhooksScreen.tsx:189-190,221).
recommend: Replace with a user-facing sentence and a Retry; and route these two screens through the shared SCREEN_ERROR treatment (shared.tsx:299-306) the other screens use.

screen: every load-error / save-error board in S7
finding: Not one of the 45 Settings boards offers a way to recover from an error: 'retry' and 'try again' appear zero times in the module.
evidence: String search across all 45 frames of section 1776:8387 for retry / try again: NO HITS. The nine load-error boards state the failure and stop — 1703:7286 'Failed to load locales.', 1703:7760 'Failed to load headers.', 1703:8394 'Failed to load redirects.', 1703:9046 'Failed to load forms.', 1703:10022, 1702:7261. Save-errors at least redisplay their save button (1703:7445 'Save locales', 1703:7914 'Save headers').
recommend: Add a Retry to every load-error state; a settings screen that can only be recovered by reloading the editor is a dead end inside a modal-free full-page surface.

finding: The two surfaces that protect a settings edit — the 'N unsaved' savebar and the discard-confirmation — have no board anywhere in the 45.
evidence: String search across all 45 frames of section 1776:8387 for 'unsaved' and 'discard': NO HITS. Code ships both: SettingsTab.tsx:883-904 savebar with unsaved count + Discard/Save, :909-986 ConfirmDialog fired by the universal dirty check at :407-411 (push, section→section and root all guarded). Every detail board instead draws a single header button ('Save changes' / 'Add domain'), which is not what the product shows once a field is touched.
recommend: Board the savebar and the discard dialog as shared states; and note that Domains and Webhooks get neither registerSaveHandler nor registerFlushHandler (SettingsTab.tsx:718,720) while still pushing dirty, so today they show two Save buttons of which one cannot work.

finding: The empty state ships an engineering note as product copy, and it contradicts the module's own main Forms board.
evidence: 1703:8882 pane text: 'A Form block renders on the published page, but its submissions are not captured yet — this inbox stays empty until that is wired.' Meanwhile 640:3135 shows three captured submissions with no caveat.
recommend: Decide which is true. If capture is unbuilt, mark the Forms family design-ahead (the module already uses [design-ahead] on 817:5289) and rewrite the empty state in the user's terms; do not ship 'until that is wired'.

screen: state naming and error voice across the six stateful screens
finding: Sibling screens use different names and different voices for the same states, so the family reads as six independent designs.
evidence: Names: Domains/Localization/Headers/Redirects/Webhooks use load-error/save-error; Forms uses 'error' (1703:9046) and 'action-error' (1703:9208) — both of which are load errors by their own copy ('Failed to load forms.' / 'Failed to load submissions.'). Voice: 'Couldn\'t load domains…' vs 'Failed to load locales.' vs the well-written Analytics validation (1703:10515: 'This doesn\'t look right. Your Google Analytics ID should start with G- followed by 10 characters, like G-ABCD123456.'). Redirects' 'save-error' (1703:8556) is a validation message ('From path must start with /'), not a save failure.
recommend: Fix the vocabulary to one set (loading / empty / load-error / save-error / validation / forbidden) and lift every error to the Analytics validation voice.

finding: State coverage is per-screen ad hoc: six screens carry 3-6 async states and six carry none, and the module never says why.
evidence: Boards: Domains 4, Forms 6, Webhooks 5, Redirects 4, Localization 3, Headers 3, Analytics 1 (validation); General, SEO, Export, Custom code, Integrations, Branding = 0. The code mostly agrees (SiteSettingsScreen has no states; Seo/Analytics/Advanced are validation-only), so the real gap is Integrations, whose OAuth connect is the most failure-prone job in the module and has neither boards nor states in IntegrationsScreen.tsx.
recommend: Record the rule on the module (validation-only screens vs server-backed screens) and add Integrations' connect/failed/revoked states if the editor keeps that screen at all.

screen: S7 · Settings · General (and SEO, Analytics, Custom code, Branding)
finding: The full-page graduation buys nothing on five screens: a 1240px pane holds a ~380px single form column, leaving roughly two thirds of the surface empty.
evidence: Measured: 638:2378 'Settings pane' x=200 w=1240 h=812; the form card in the screenshot spans roughly x=232→994 of 1440 and stops at y≈560 of 900. Same shape on 638:3070, 639:3443, 639:4144, 1138:13436.
recommend: Either use the width (two columns, or preview beside form as Export already does) or return these screens to a narrower measure; a form column adrift in 1240px reads as an unfinished page.

finding: Every Settings board keeps the canvas-selection footer while no canvas is on screen, so it reports a selection the user cannot see.
evidence: All 45 frames end with 'Section · Hero | 680 × 250 | Desktop · 100%' (measured on 638:2378: Footer x=0 y=868 w=1440 h=32 with those three text nodes). Settings is mode:'fullpage' (tabsConfig.ts:198) and replaces the canvas region entirely.
recommend: Blank or repurpose the footer in full-page mode — the code's own footer already prints 'Nothing selected' and 'Loading…' variants (StudioFooter.tsx:171-177), so a settings variant is cheap.

finding: The root's 13 rows carry no icons and no state, so a 13-item list is differentiated only by two lines of text; the code's icons do not help either because 8 of the 13 share one glyph.
evidence: 1688:7195 rows are title + subtitle + chevron only (verified in the board screenshot). Code: SettingsTab.tsx:81-91 — export, domains, analytics, localization, custom-code, redirects, headers, forms, integrations and webhooks all pass IntegrationsIcon.
recommend: Give each row a distinct icon, and show the state that matters on the row (domain connected / N redirects / N new submissions / locked) so the list is scannable.

finding: Only one of the two plan-gated screens has a lock board, and no board shows the lock before the click.
evidence: SCREEN_PLAN_REQUIREMENTS (types.ts:70-73) gates custom-code AND integrations. Boards: 1138:13436 exists for Custom code; there is no Integrations lock board in section 1776:8387. The nav on every board shows no Pro badge although SettingsTab.tsx:767 renders one. types.ts:61-69 also records that this table was keyed to an id no screen has, so Custom code rendered ungated for months.
recommend: Board the Integrations lock, and draw the nav Pro badge — a paywall the user only meets after navigating is the most expensive kind.

verdict: MERGE-INTO(their parent screens as component states)
finding: 26 of the module's 45 boards are async variants of six screens, each redrawn as a complete 1440x900 shell carrying a full 25-edge copy of the nav — 58% of the module maintains chrome, not design.
evidence: Frame census of 1776:8387: 26 frames named '· loading / empty / load-error / save-error / …', each 1440x900 with out-degree 25-27, of which ~24 edges are the nav duplicated on every board. Their in-degree is 1 each (only the parent screen links to them).
recommend: Draw the six pane states as component variants against one shell frame; the shell is identical on all 26 and the diff is a single card.

verdict: UNSURE(right job, wrong module and wrong surface)
finding: A site-health monitor is filed inside Settings but is not in the Settings nav, and the product's actual door for it opens the dashboard, not an editor panel.
evidence: Its 13-row nav (1688:7195) contains no Health row. Incoming edges: from 642:3401 'Site menu (⋯)' via a hotspot named 'menu · Site health', and from 817:4950 / 1157:4593 'Preview · performance audit'. Code: SiteMenu.tsx:222 'Site health' opens a NEW TAB at ${DASHBOARD_URL}/dashboard/sites/<id>#site-health. The board draws an 800x480 in-editor panel (uptime, avg response, errors, bandwidth, incident list, 'Alert on downtime: Email + Slack').
recommend: Move the pair to whichever module owns the dashboard site page, or add a Health row to the Settings nav and build the in-editor panel — right now the design and the product disagree about where this lives.

finding: The SEO board draws two controls the editor does not own — 'Allow search indexing' and an editable robots.txt — while omitting the canonical URL. The only door for all three is the dashboard.
evidence: 638:3070 INDEXING block: 'Allow search indexing' toggle + robots.txt textarea ('User-agent: * / Allow: / / Sitemap: …'). Code: SeoScreen.tsx has title template, twitter handle and default OG image only; robotsTxt / allowIndexing / site canonicalUrl have 0 editor hits and live at packages/dashboard/components/site-detail/seo-tab.tsx:133-190, whose own comment (:104-105) calls them 'server-side knobs the editor doesn\'t own'.
recommend: Either mark this block design-ahead and plan the editor procedures, or cut it from the board and add a ↗ row — a boarded toggle with no writer is how a feature ships looking finished and doing nothing.

verdict: UNSURE(the screen designs a product that has no other screen)
finding: The board promises translation management — per-locale page counts and a LIVE / PENDING / NOT STARTED workflow — but there is no screen anywhere for actually translating a page, and the three procedures that would do it have no caller.
evidence: 639:3795 table: 'LOCALE | PATH | PAGES TRANSLATED | STATUS · English / 6 of 6 / LIVE · French /fr / 4 of 6 / PENDING · Arabic /ar / 0 of 6 / NOT STARTED'. Code: LocalizationScreen.tsx writes only defaultLocale and enabledLocales; server/trpc/routers/pages.ts:71,77,90 (getTranslation / setTranslation / removeTranslation) have no UI caller. No board in the file names a translation editor.
recommend: Design the per-page translation job (where does '4 of 6' get to 6?) or reduce this screen to locale declaration and drop the progress column — a progress bar with no way to advance it is a promise the product cannot keep.

finding: The board draws a Cookie Consent toggle whose value nothing reads, on a product that injects a tracking beacon into every published page with no consent check at all.
evidence: 639:3443 CONSENT block with a 'Cookie Consent' toggle. Code: AnalyticsScreen.tsx:280-286 writes analytics.cookieConsent and it is read by nothing (the screen discloses this at :287-299); lib/publish-html.ts:22-28 injects a first-party localStorage + sendBeacon tracker into every published page unconditionally.
recommend: Either wire the toggle to the beacon and the third-party tags, or remove it from the board; and design the consent banner itself, which has no screen in this file.

screen: site lifecycle jobs with no board and no editor door
finding: Seven site-level jobs a site owner plausibly needs have no board in this 45-screen module and no editor door: delete, duplicate, transfer, site password, backups, slug, and sharing/access.
evidence: All exist as dashboard surfaces or procedures with zero editor callers: site password / touch icon / slug at packages/dashboard/components/site-detail/settings-tab.tsx:192-198,232; siteDetail.sharing.* has 0 editor callers; no backups procedure; templates.cloneFromSite (server/trpc/routers/templates.ts:17) — 'save this site as a template' — has no entry point anywhere in either app.
recommend: Decide per job: WORKSPACE ↗ row (like Members/Billing) or an editor screen. Today the answer is silence, and silence is what produced an orphan procedure.

finding: The nav and the board promise a '404 suggester' and the board shows two accepted suggestions, but nothing in the product produces or stores a custom 404 or a sitemap.
evidence: 640:2440 '404 SUGGESTER · Suggest redirects from 404s · /pizza-menu → /menu · Accept'; nav subtitle '301 / 302 + 404 suggester' (also SettingsTab.tsx:87). No tRPC procedure exists for sitemap or a custom 404. The editor also lacks the dashboard's update / import_csv / export_csv on redirects (site-detail/redirects-tab.tsx:125,149,154,161).
recommend: Either board where the 404 data comes from, or drop the suggester from the board and the subtitle until it has a source.

screen: permission and failure states missing from Domains
finding: Webhooks got a 'forbidden' board; Domains, which has the same kind of role restriction plus a second failure path, got neither.
evidence: Code: DomainsScreen.tsx:222,287 disables the connect and remove controls with a reason tooltip for insufficient role; :159 routes a remove failure into loadError, so it renders at the top of the section rather than at the row acted on. Boards for Domains: loading, empty, load-error, save-error only (1702:6931/7095/7261/7425).
recommend: Add a role-disabled board and a remove-failure board for Domains, and place the remove error on the row — the current code puts it where the user is not looking.

screen: the save pill on all 12 full-shell Shell boards
finding: The shell's single most important status indicator reads 'Saved 2m ago' on every board — including Loading, Offline, AI agent run, First run, and the board literally named 'Saving → conflict'.
evidence: Topbar text read on all 12 full-shell frames of 1776:8385: 65:2, 65:211, 65:412, 66:4, 66:225, 66:441, 66:640, 199:2, 199:205, 199:409, 200:2, 200:213, 202:2, 642:3696 — every one contains 'Saved 2m ago'. 65:2 is a brand-new project that has never been saved. Code ships six distinct states with distinct copy and colour (chrome-ui/SaveStatus.tsx:41-52): Saved · 2m ago / Saving… / Unsaved changes (a button) / Save failed — retry (red) / Offline — not saved (yellow) / Conflict — reload (yellow), with precedence at StudioHeader.tsx:552-562.
recommend: Redraw the pill per state on at least Loading, Offline, Saving→conflict and AI run; and add the missing 'Unsaved changes' and 'Save failed' shell states — five of the six shipped save states have no board.

screen: Shell state 11 · Saving → conflict — the scrim
finding: The conflict scrim is named rgba(15,23,42,.4) and measures fully opaque #111827, so the dialog blacks out the entire editor and the user cannot see which page or element the conflict is about.
evidence: Measured on 66:640 children: 'scrim rgba(15,23,42,.4)' — nodeOpacity=1, fills=SOLID opacity=1, colour rgb(17,24,39). Both the alpha and the hex differ from the layer's own name (15,23,42 = #0F172A). Confirmed in the board screenshot: nothing of the shell is visible behind the modal.
recommend: Set the fill to the named token value and the alpha to 0.4 — a conflict dialog is exactly the moment the user needs to see what is at stake.

finding: The dialog's three actions do not match the shipped ones, and the destructive one is a single click carrying the same visual weight as the safe one.
evidence: Board: 'Someone else saved first' / 'Sara saved a change to this page 40 seconds ago. Keeping yours will overwrite hers.' with Review both · Save backup · Keep mine — the last two both filled blue. Code (modals/ConflictModal.tsx:35, rendered AquibraStudio.tsx:684-708): Reload latest / Save a backup (downloads JSON, then reloads) / Overwrite… as a deliberate two-step confirm.
recommend: Redraw to the shipped three, keep the two-step on overwrite, and give exactly one action primary weight — 'Keep mine' as a filled button next to another filled button invites the one click that destroys a colleague's work.

finding: The Shell section holds the happy path and almost nothing else: four genuine shell states are filed under Journeys, and the module's most consequential dialog is filed under Notes.
evidence: Full-shell 1440x900 frames with the same six-tool rail, filed in 1776:8388 Journeys: 297:2139 'S1.2 · load-error' and 297:2027 'S1.2 · crash-recovery'. Also outside Shell: 294:1976 + 1347:7162 session-expired (Journeys), 815:4518 keyboard-shortcuts-overlay (Journeys), 307:2223 recovery banner (Reference 862:6859), 1172:4804 exit guard (Notes 1776:8389). Each maps to real shell code: LoadErrorBanner.tsx:33,53 (three kinds), StudioErrorBoundary AquibraStudio.tsx:82-134, SessionExpiredModal.tsx:85, KeyboardShortcutsPanel via StudioModals.tsx:169.
recommend: Move these six into Shell. A designer who opens 'Shell · 17 screens' today cannot see how the editor fails, which is the half of the shell that matters most.

finding: The exit guard — three dialogs whose copy matches the code exactly — lives in the Notes annotation section, where the file's own convention says only captions belong.
evidence: 1172:4804 children: dirty (420x104), risky-offline (420x117), stranded (420x117), with copy 'Leave with unsaved changes?', 'You\'re offline with unsaved changes', 'Some changes are only on this device — 2 changes haven\'t reached the server yet.' Code: StudioHeader.tsx:393-419 guardNavigation with exactly those three kinds, dialog at :945-1012. Its only inbound edge is from 927:4474; the ‹ Exit button in the topbar carries a reaction on exactly ONE of the 17 Shell boards.
recommend: Move it into Shell and wire the topbar exit button to it on the Shell boards; the guard is currently unreachable from every screen it protects.

finding: A documentation artifact is filed as a product screen: it has annotation chips drawn into the frame, one inbound edge from the Reference index, and it asserts a drawer model the code removed.
evidence: 963:4474 screenshot shows two orange/blue annotation badges baked into the canvas: 'Drawer slot · 320 · pinned, pushes canvas' and 'Overlay · 360 · floats, does not take the drawer slot'. In-degree 1, from 876:4532 'Reference · index'; out-degree 59, acting as a hub. Code: the drawerPinned overlay mode was removed 2026-09-04 (LayoutShell.tsx:267-272), and 202:2 is already annotated RETIRED for the same pin behaviour.
recommend: Rename with a REFERENCE prefix and move it beside 876:4532; and correct the 320 figure, which no longer matches the shipped drawer.

finding: The loading board contradicts itself: the canvas shows skeletons and the footer says 'Loading…', while the right inspector is fully populated with a selected element's values and the left drawer is blank white with no skeleton at all.
evidence: 65:412 screenshot: inspector shows Section / Display / Size Fill·Hug / Padding 24,16 / Gap 16 / Family Inter Tight / Size 14,1.5 / Fill #1A56DB / Radius 8 / Opacity 100 — the identical block copy-pasted from 199:205 — while the footer reads 'Loading…' (which matches StudioFooter.tsx:171) and the topbar reads 'Saved 2m ago · In review · 3 open'.

verdict: KEEP(rename — it is not a 403 gate)

screen: how modals are represented across the module
finding: The module represents modals three different ways, so there is no reusable answer to 'how does an overlay sit in the shell'.
evidence: 66:640 draws the conflict as a full 1440x900 shell plus scrim plus card; 1175:4804 (420x225) and 927:4474 (520x216) and 1172:4867 (560x244) are bare cards with no shell and no scrim.
recommend: Pick one convention — a card with a documented scrim token, shown once in context — and apply it to all four.

screen: page tabs carry a close affordance
finding: Every page tab shows an ✕, which implies a page can be closed — but a site builder has no closed-page state; a page is either in the site or deleted.
evidence: 199:205 (and 66:441, 66:225, 200:2, 200:213, 199:409) all read 'Home | ✕ | Menu | ✕ | Contact | ✕'. The tab bar lives inside the canvas region (StudioPanels.tsx:488, PageTabBar).
recommend: Either drop the ✕ or say what it does; if it closes a tab without touching the page, the design must show how a closed page is reopened.

verdict: UNSURE(needs a live measurement, not a redraw)
finding: The only sub-1440 Shell board is retired, and the one responsive rule in the code looks broken — so nothing in design or code covers the widths real laptops use.
evidence: 202:2 'Shell · 1280 · pin auto-released (overlay) — RETIRED 2026-09-04' is the module's only non-1440 frame. Code: the single shell breakpoint is LayoutShell.css:323 @media (max-width:1366px), which floats the inspector (:341-350) but is outranked on the grid-column rule by .layout-shell--has-sidebar.layout-shell--inspector-open (:183, 0-2-0 vs 0-1-0) — media queries add no specificity — so a 300px empty gutter should remain beside a floating inspector. LayoutShell.css:354 @media (max-width:1024px) is an empty block whose comment defers to a component that does not exist.
recommend: Measure the editor live at 1366 and 1280 before drawing anything; if the gutter is real, this is a shell defect the design has no board for at all.
